Vendor profile

Dassault Systèmes

Dassault Systèmes SE (Euronext: DSY) — Architect of CATIA, SOLIDWORKS, the CGM Geometric Modeler & the 3DEXPERIENCE PLM Platform

By GstarCAD Academy Engineering Editorial Board (Suzhou Gstarsoft Co., Ltd.) Reviewed by GstarCAD Academy Editorial Team Last reviewed 2026-10-26 Editorial Process

1. Aerospace Origins: From Mirage Fighter Surface Mathematics to Global PLM Dominance

Spun out of Avions Marcel Dassault in 1981 in Vélizy-Villacoublay, France by a team of aerospace engineers led by Francis Bernard (creator of the 3D surface program GECAO), Dassault Systèmes SE (Euronext: DSY) revolutionized freeform surface modeling with CATIA. Early partnerships with IBM allowed CATIA V3 and V4 to become the undisputed standard for commercial aircraft (Boeing 777—the world's first 100% digitally pre-assembled airliner) and automotive Class-A body-in-white engineering.

In 1997, Dassault Systèmes acquired SOLIDWORKS for $310M in stock, capturing the mainstream Windows mechanical CAD market. Subsequent acquisitions—including Abaqus Inc. (2005, forming SIMULIA), MatrixOne (2006, forming ENOVIA), and Delmia—culminated in the launch of the unified 3DEXPERIENCE Platform in 2012.

2. Dual-Kernel Architecture: Convergence Geometric Modeler (CGM) vs. Parasolid

A critical engineering nuance when exchanging 3D assemblies across the Dassault portfolio is that CATIA and desktop SOLIDWORKS do not share the same geometric kernel:

  • Convergence Geometric Modeler (CGM): Developed in-house by Dassault Systèmes for CATIA V5/V6 and 3DEXPERIENCE apps, CGM excels at high-degree C2/C3 curvature-continuous Bézier and NURBS surface patches, large-scale aerospace kinematics, and hybrid polyhedral/exact B-Rep operators.
  • Parasolid Kernel (Licensed from Siemens): Desktop SOLIDWORKS (.sldprt, .sldasm) continues to run on the Parasolid kernel with a strict $10^{-8}\,\text{m}$ modeling tolerance. Converting complex fillets between SOLIDWORKS (Parasolid) and CATIA (CGM) requires healing edge tolerances or utilizing direct 3D Interconnect translators.

3. Shop-Floor 2D DWG Downstream Workflow with GstarCAD Mechanical

In automotive Tier-1 suppliers and precision machinery plants using CATIA or SOLIDWORKS for 3D master modeling, equipping hundreds of shop-floor CNC programmers, quality inspectors, and tooling subcontractors with 3DEXPERIENCE seats is financially prohibitive. Best-practice enterprises export 2D manufacturing views to native DWG and standardize downstream detailing on GstarCAD Mechanical and FastView 3D (which natively reads .catpart, .sldprt, and STEP AP242 without a Dassault license).

5. Enterprise Co-Existence, Migration & TCO Optimization Protocol

In production supply chains where upstream 3D models or BIM containers originate from Dassault Systèmes SE (Vélizy-Villacoublay, France — Euronext: DSY) platforms, engineering IT directors optimize total cost of ownership (TCO) by deploying a tiered seat architecture centered on GstarCAD 2027 and DWG FastView:

  • Verified Data Exchange Pipeline: View native CATIA V5/V6 (.CATPart/.CATProduct) directly on shop floors with FastView 3D, and offload 2D stamping die, welding jig, and factory layout drafting to GstarCAD Mechanical 2027.
  • Eliminating Redundant Seat Rentals: Rather than purchasing high-cost authoring subscriptions for project managers, site engineers, estimators, CNC operators, and quality inspectors who primarily review geometry or annotate 2D DWG/DXF sheets, organizations equip 70%–80% of their workforce with GstarCAD Perpetual Floating Licenses (GstarLM) and FastView 3D.
  • Automated Database Hygiene Before Transmittal: Prior to archiving project deliverables or importing external vendor DWG exports into corporate PDM/CDE vaults, run GstarCAD's batch script sequence (-PURGE RegApps → OVERKILL → AUDIT Yes → INDEXCTL = 3) to guarantee sub-second opening times and zero proxy object corruption.
